=== #1 | Laparoscopic Gastric Bypass | Bariatrics ===
1. The patient was taken to the operating room and placed supine on the operating room table.
2. All pressure points were carefully padded.
3. She was given general anesthesia with endotracheal intubation.
4. SCD stockings were placed on both legs.
5. Foley catheter was placed for bladder decompression.
6. The abdomen was then prepped and draped in standard sterile surgical fashion.
7. Marcaine was then injected through umbilicus.
8. A small incision was made.
9. A Veress needle was introduced into the abdomen.
10. CO2 insufflation was done to a maximum pressure of 15 mmHg.
11. A 12-mm VersaStep port was placed through the umbilicus.
12. I then placed a 5-mm port just anterior to the midaxillary line and just subcostal on the right side.
13. I placed another 5-mm port in the midclavicular line just subcostal on the right side, a few centimeters below and medial to that, I placed a 12-mm VersaStep port.
14. On the left side, just anterior to the midaxillary line and just subcostal, I placed a 5-mm port.
15. A few centimeters below and medial to that, I placed a 15-mm port.
16. I began by lifting up the omentum and identifying the transverse colon and lifting that up and thereby identifying my ligament of Treitz.
17. I ran the small bowel down approximately 40 cm and divided the small bowel with a white load GIA stapler.
18. I then divided the mesentery all the way down to the base of the mesentery with a LigaSure device.
19. I then ran the distal bowel down, approximately 100 cm, and at 100 cm, I made a hole at the antimesenteric portion of the Roux limb and a hole in the antimesenteric portion of the duodenogastric limb, and I passed a 45 white load stapler and fired a stapler creating a side-to-side anastomosis.
20. I reapproximated the edges of the defect.
21. I lifted it up and stapled across it with another white load stapler.
22. I then closed the mesenteric defect with interrupted Surgidac sutures.
23. I divided the omentum all the way down to the colon in order to create a passageway for my small bowel to go antecolic.
24. I then put the patient in reverse Trendelenburg.
25. I placed a liver retractor, identified, and dissected the angle of His.
26. I then dissected on the lesser curve, approximately 2.5 cm below the gastroesophageal junction, and got into a lesser space.
27. I fired transversely across the stomach with a 45 blue load stapler.
28. I then used two fires of the 60 blue load with SeamGuard to go up into my angle of His, thereby creating my gastric pouch.
29. I then made a hole at the base of the gastric pouch and had Anesthesia remove the bougie and place the OG tube connected to the anvil.
30. I pulled the anvil into place, and I then opened up my 15-mm port site and passed my EEA stapler.
31. I passed that in the end of my Roux limb and had the spike come out antimesenteric.
32. I joined the spike with the anvil and fired a stapler creating an end-to-side anastomosis, then divided across the redundant portion of my Roux limb with a white load GI stapler, and removed it with an Endocatch bag.
33. I put some additional 2-0 Vicryl sutures in the anastomosis for further security.
34. I then placed a bowel clamp across the bowel.
35. I went above and passed an EGD scope into the mouth down to the esophagus and into the gastric pouch.
36. I distended gastric pouch with air.
37. There was no air leak seen.
38. I could pass the scope easily through the anastomosis.
39. There was no bleeding seen through the scope.
40. We closed the 15-mm port site with interrupted 0 Vicryl suture utilizing Carter-Thomason.
41. I copiously irrigated out that incision with about 2 L of saline.
42. I then closed the skin of all incisions with running Monocryl.
43. Sponge, instrument, and needle counts were correct at the end of the case.
44. The patient tolerated the procedure well without any complications.

=== #2 | Liposuction | Bariatrics ===
1. The patient was taken to the operating room and placed in the supine position.
2. Following adequate induction of general LMA anesthesia, the chest and abdomen was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.
3. The supraumbilical abdomen was then injected with a solution of 5% lidocaine with epinephrine, as was the dog ear.
4. At this time, the superior central scar was then excised, dissection continued through the subcutaneous tissue, the underlying latissimus muscle until the capsule of the implant was reached.
5. This was then opened.
6. The implant was removed and placed on the back table in antibiotic solution.
7. Using Bovie cautery, the medial capsule was released and undermining was then performed with release of the muscle to the level of the proposed medial projection of the breast.
8. The inframammary fold medially was secured with 2-0 PDS suture to create greater takeoff point at this level which in the upright position and using a sizer produced a good form.
9. The lateral pocket was diminished by series of 2-0 PDS suture to provide medialization of the implant.
10. The implant was then placed back into the submuscular pocket with much improved positioning and medial fullness.
11. With this completed, the implant was again removed, antibiotic irrigation was performed.
12. A drain was placed and brought out through a separate inferior stab wound incision and hemostasis was confirmed.
13. The implant was then replaced and the wound was then closed in layers using 2-0 PDS running suture on the muscle and 3-0 Monocryl Dermabond subcuticular sutures.
14. The 2.5 cm dog ear was then excised into and including the subcutaneous tissue, even contouring was achieved and this was closed with two layers using 3-0 Monocryl suture.
15. Using a #3 cannula, a superior umbilical incision, liposuction was carried out into the supraumbilical abdomen, removing approximately 40 to 50 mL of fat with improved supraumbilical contours.
16. This was closed with 6-0 Prolene suture.
17. The patient was placed in a compressive garment after treating the incision with Dermabond, Steri-Strips and antibiotic ointment around the drain site and umbilicus.
18. A Kerlix dressing and a surgical bra was placed to the chest area.
19. A compressive garment was placed.
20. The patient was then aroused from anesthesia, extubated, and taken to the recovery room in stable condition.
21. Sponge, needle, lap, instrument counts were all correct.
22. The patient tolerated the procedure well.
23. There were no complications.
24. The estimated blood loss was approximately 25 mL.

=== #4 | Bony Impacted Teeth Removal | Dentistry ===
1. Patient was brought to the operating room, placed on the table in a supine position, and after demonstration of an adequate plane of general anesthesia via the nasotracheal route, patient was prepped and draped in the usual fashion for an intraoral procedure.
2. A gauze throat pack was placed and local anesthetic was administered in all four quadrants, a total of 7.2 mL of lidocaine 2% with 1:100,000 epinephrine, and 3.6 mL of bupivacaine 0.5% with 1:200,000 epinephrine.
3. Beginning on the upper right tooth #1, incision was made with a #15 blade.
4. Envelope flap was raised with the periosteal elevator, and bone was removed on the buccal aspect with straight elevator.
5. Potts elevator was then used to luxate the tooth from the socket.
6. Remnants of the follicle were then removed with hemostat.
7. The area was irrigated and then closed with 3-0 gut suture.
8. On the lower right tooth #32, incision was made with a #15 blade.
9. Envelope flap was raised with the periosteal elevator, and bone was removed on the buccal and distal aspect with a high-speed drill with a round bur.
10. Tooth was then sectioned with the bur and removed in several pieces.
11. Remnants of the follicle were removed with a curved hemostat.
12. The area was irrigated with normal saline solution and closed with 3-0 gut sutures.
13. Moving to #16 on the upper left, incision was made with a #15 blade.
14. Envelope flap was raised with the periosteal elevator, and bone was removed on the buccal aspect with straight elevator.
15. Potts elevator was then used to luxate the tooth from the socket.
16. Remnants of the follicle were removed with a curved hemostat.
17. The area was irrigated with normal saline solution and closed with 3-0 gut sutures.
18. Moving to the lower left #17, incision was made with a #15 blade.
19. Envelope flap was raised with the periosteal elevator, and bone was removed on the buccal and distal aspect with high-speed drill with a round bur.
20. Then the bur was used to section the tooth vertically.
21. Tooth was removed in several pieces followed by the removal of the remnants of the follicle.
22. The area was irrigated with normal saline solution and closed with 3-0 gut sutures.
23. Upon completion of the procedure, the throat pack was removed and the pharynx was suctioned.
24. An NG tube was then inserted and small amount of gastric contents were suctioned.
25. Patient was then awakened, extubated, and taken to the PACU in stable condition.

=== #10 | Transurethral Resection Of Bladder Tumor | Urology ===
1. After preoperative counseling of the patient and his wife, the patient was taken to the operating room and administered a spinal anesthetic.
2. He was placed in lithotomy position and prepped and draped in the usual fashion.
3. Using the visual obturator, the resectoscope was then inserted per urethra into the bladder.
4. The bladder was inspected confirming previous cystoscopic findings of a 2.5- to 3-cm left lateral wall bladder tumor away from the ureteral orifice.
5. Using the resectoscope loop, the tumor was then resected down to its base in a stepwise fashion.
6. Following completion of resection down to the base, the bladder was _______ free of tumor specimen.
7. The resectoscope was then reinserted and the base of the bladder tumor was then resected to get the base of the bladder tumor specimen, this was sent as a separate pathological specimen.
8. Hemostasis was assured with electrocautery.
9. The base of the tumor was then fulgurated again and into the periphery out in the normal mucosa surrounding the base of the bladder tumor.
10. Following completion of the fulguration, there was good hemostasis.
11. The remainder of the bladder was without evidence of significant abnormality.
12. Both ureteral orifices were visualized and noted to drain freely of clear urine.
13. The bladder was filled and the resectoscope was removed.
14. A 22-French 3-way Foley catheter was inserted per urethra into the bladder.
15. The balloon was inflated to 30 mL.
16. The catheter with sterile continuous irrigation and was noted to drain clear irrigant.
17. The patient was then removed from lithotomy position.
18. He was in stable condition.

7. The anterior urethra was normal without strictures or lesions.
8. The bladder was severely trabeculated with multiple bladder diverticula.
9. There is a very bladder diverticula located in the right posterior bladder wall just proximal to the trigone.
10. Using the ***** resection apparatus and a right angle resection loop, the prostate was resected initially at the area of the median lobe.
11. Once the median lobe has completely resected, the left lateral lobe and then the right lateral lobes were taken down.
12. Once an adequate channel had been achieved, the prostatic specimen was retrieved from the bladder by using an Ellik evacuator.

=== #14 | Salvage Cystectomy | Urology ===
1. The patient was brought to the operative suite and after adequate general endotracheal and epidural anesthesia obtained, placed in the supine position, flexed over the anterosuperior iliac spine, and his abdomen and genitalia were sterilely prepped and draped in the usual fashion.

5. Moist wound towels and a Bookwalter retractor were placed for exposure.
6. We began by retracting the bowels by mobilizing the cecum and ascending colon and hepatic flexure and elevating the terminal ileum up to the second and third portion of the duodenum.
7. The ureter was identified as a crisis over the iliac vessels and dissected deep into pelvis and subsequently divided between clips.
8. An identical procedure was performed in the left side with similar findings and the bowels were packed cephalad.,We began then dissecting the bladder away from the pelvic side walls staying medial to both epigastric arteries.
9. This was quite challenging because of the previous radiation therapy and radical prostatectomy.
10. We essentially carved the bladder off of the pelvic sidewall inferiorly as best we could and then we were able to have enough freedom to identify the lateral pedicles, and these were taken between double clips approximately and clipped distally.
11. We then approached things posteriorly and carefully dissected between the __________ and posterior bladder.
12. There was some remnant seminal vesicle on the right as well as both remnant ejaculatory duct and we used this to dissect the longus safe plane anterior to the rectum.
13. We then entered the bladder anteriorly as distal as we could and remove the bladder and what we thought was a bladder neck and this appeared to end in a diverticulum.
14. We then peeled it off the remaining rectum and passed the specimen off the operative field.
15. Bladder was irrigated with warm sterile water and a meticulous inspection was made for hemostasis.,We then completely mobilized the omentum off of the proximal transverse colon.
16. This allowed a generous flap to be able to be laid into the pelvis without tension.,We then turned our attention to forming the Indiana pouch.
17. I completed the dissection of the right hepatic flexure and the proximal transverse colon and mobilized the omentum off of this portion of the colon.
18. The colon was divided proximal to the middle colic using a GIA-80 stapler.
19. I then divided the avascular plane of Treves along the terminal ileum and selected a point approximately 15 cm proximal to the ileocecal valve to divide the ileum.
20. The mesentery was then sealed with a LigaSure device and divided, and the bowel was divided with a GIA-60 stapler.
21. We then performed a side-to-side ileo-transverse colostomy using a GIA-80 stapler, closing the open end with a TA 60.
22. The angles were reinforced with silk sutures and the mesenteric closed with interrupted silk sutures.,We then removed the staple line along the terminal ileum, passed a 12-French Robinson catheter into the cecal segment, and plicated the ileum with 3 firings of the GIA-60 stapler.
23. The ileocecal valve was then reinforced with interrupted 3-0 silk sutures as described by Rowland, et al, and following this, passage of an 18-French Robinson catheter was associated with the characteristic "pop," indicating that we had adequately plicated the ileocecal valve.,As the patient had had a previous appendectomy, we made an opening in the cecum in the area of the previous appendectomy.
24. We then removed the distal staple line along the transverse colon and aligned the cecal end and the distal middle colic end with two 3-0 Vicryl sutures.
25. The bowel segment was then folded over on itself and the reservoir formed with 3 successive applications of the SGIA Polysorb-75.
26. Between the staple lines, Vicryl sutures were placed and the defects closed with 3-0 Vicryl suture ligatures.,We then turned our attention to forming the ileocolonic anastomosis.
27. The left ureter was mobilized and brought underneath the sigmoid mesentery and brought through the mesentery of the terminal ileum and an end-to-side anastomosis performed with an open technique using interrupted 4-0 Vicryl sutures, and this was stented with a Cook 8.4-French ureteral stent, and this was secured to the bowel lumen with a 5-0 chromic suture.
28. The right ureter was brought underneath the pouch and placed in a stented fashion with an identical anastomosis.
29. We then brought the stents out through a separate incision cephalad in the pouch and they were secured with a 2-0 chromic suture.
30. A 24-French Malecot catheter was placed through the cecum and secured with a chromic suture.
31. The staple lines were then buried with a running 3-0 Vicryl two-layer suture and the open end of the pouch closed with a TA 60 Polysorb suture.
32. The pouch was filled to 240 cc and noted to be watertight, and the ureteral anastomoses were intact.,We then made a final inspection for hemostasis.
33. The cecostomy tube was then brought out to the right lower quadrant and secured to the skin with silk sutures.
34. We then matured our stoma through the umbilicus.
35. We removed the plug of skin through the umbilicus and delivered the ileal segment through this.
36. A portion of the ileum was removed and healthy, well-vascularized tissue was matured with interrupted 3-0 chromic sutures.
37. We left an 18-French Robinson through the stomag and secured this to the skin with silk sutures.
38. The Malecot and stents were also secured in a similar fashion.,We matured the stoma to the umbilicus with interrupted chromic stitches.

40. A Large JP drain was placed in the pelvis dependent to the omentum pedicle flap as well as the Indiana pouch.,The rectus fascia was closed with a buried #2 Prolene running stitch, tying a new figure-of-eight proximally and distally and meeting in the middle and tying it underneath the fascia.
41. Subcutaneous tissue was irrigated with saline and skin was closed with surgical clips.
42. The estimated blood loss was 450 mL, and the patient received no packed red blood cells.
43. The final sponge and needle count were reported to be correct.
44. The patient was awakened and extubated, and taken on stretcher to the recovery room in satisfactory condition.

3. We used a #10-blade scalpel to make a midline median sternotomy incision.

6. The chest retractor was positioned.
7. Next, full-dose heparin was given.
8. The pericardium was opened.
9. Pericardial stay sutures were positioned.
10. After obtaining adequate ACT, we prepared to place the patient on cardiopulmonary bypass.
11. A 2-0 double pursestring of Ethibond suture was placed in the ascending aorta.
12. Through this was passed an aortic cannula connected to the arterial side of the cardiopulmonary bypass machine.
13. Next a 3-0 Prolene pursestring was placed in the right atrial appendage.
14. Through this was passed our venous cannula connected to the venous portion of the cardiopulmonary bypass machine.
15. A 4-0 U-stitch was placed in the right atrium.
16. A retrograde cardioplegia catheter was positioned at this site.
17. Next, scissors were used to dissect out the right upper pulmonary vein.
18. A 4-0 Prolene pursestring was placed in the right upper pulmonary vein.
19. Next, a right-angle sump was placed at this position.
20. We then connected our retrograde cardioplegia catheter to the cardioplegia solution circuit.
21. Bovie electrocautery was used to dissect the interface between the aorta and pulmonary artery.
22. The aorta was completely encircled.
23. Next, an antegrade cardioplegia needle and associated sump were placed in the ascending aorta.
24. We then prepared to cross-clamp the aorta.
25. We went down on our flows and cross-clamped the aorta.
26. We backed up our flows.
27. We then gave antegrade and retrograde cold blood cardioplegia solution circuit so as to arrest the heart.
28. The patient had some aortic insufficiency so we elected, after initially arresting the heart, to open the aorta and transect it and then give direct ostial infusion of cardioplegia solution circuit.
29. Next, after obtaining complete diastolic arrest of the heart, we turned our attention to exposing the aortic valve, and 4-0 Tycron sutures were placed in the commissures.
30. In addition, a 2-0 Prolene suture was placed in the aortic wall so as to bring the aortic wall and root up into view.
31. Next, scissors were used to excise the diseased aortic valve leaflets.
32. Care was taken to remove all the calcium from the aortic annulus.
33. We then sized up the aortic annulus which came out to be a **-mm stentless porcine Toronto valve.
34. We prepared the valve.
35. Next, we placed our proximal suture line of interrupted 4-0 Tycron sutures for the annulus.
36. We started with our individual commissural stitches.
37. They were connected to our valve sewing ring.
38. Next, we placed 5 interrupted 4-0 Tycron sutures in a subannular fashion at each commissural position.
39. After doing so, we passed 1 end of the suture through the sewing portion of the Toronto stentless porcine valve.
40. The valve was lowered into place and all of the sutures were tied.
41. Next, we gave another round of cold blood antegrade and retrograde cardioplegia.
42. Next, we sewed our distal suture line.
43. We began with the left coronary cusp of the valve.
44. We ran a 5-0 RB needle up both sides of the valve.
45. Care was taken to avoid the left coronary ostia.
46. This procedure was repeated on the right cusp of the stentless porcine valve.
47. Again, care was taken to avoid any injury to the coronary ostia.
48. Lastly, we sewed our non-coronary cusp.
49. This was done without difficulty.
50. At this point we inspected our aortic valve.
51. There was good coaptation of the leaflets, and it was noted that both the left and the right coronary ostia were open.
52. We gave another round of cold blood antegrade and retrograde cardioplegia.
53. The antegrade portion was given in a direct ostial fashion once again.
54. We now turned our attention to closing the aorta.
55. A 4-0 Prolene double row of suture was used to close the aorta in a running fashion.
56. Just prior to closing, we de-aired the heart and gave a warm shot of antegrade and retrograde cardioplegia.
57. At this point, we removed our aortic cross-clamp.
58. The heart gradually regained its electromechanical activity.
59. We placed 2 atrial and 2 ventricular pacing wires.
60. We removed our aortic vent and oversewed that site with another 4-0 Prolene on an SH needle.
61. We removed our retrograde cardioplegia catheter.
62. We oversewed that site with a 5-0 Prolene.
63. By now, the heart was de-aired and resumed normal electromechanical activity.
64. We began to wean the patient from cardiopulmonary bypass.
65. We then removed our venous cannula and suture ligated that site with a #2 silk.
66. We then gave full-dose protamine.
67. After knowing that there was no evidence of a protamine reaction, we removed the aortic cannula.
68. We buttressed that site with a 4-0 Prolene on an SH needle.
69. We placed a mediastinal chest tube and brought it out through the skin.
70. We also placed 2 Blake drains, 1 in the left chest and 1 in the right chest, as the patient had some bilateral pleural effusions.
71. They were brought out through the skin.
72. The sternum was closed with #7 wires in an interrupted figure-of-eight fashion.
73. The fascia was closed with #1 Vicryl.
74. We closed the subcu tissue with 2-0 Vicryl and the skin with 4-0 PDS.

=== #229 | ORIF - 2 | Surgery ===
1. Open reduction and internal fixation, high grade Frykman VIII distal radius fracture.,ANESTHESIA: , General endotracheal.,PREOPERATIVE INDICATIONS: , This is a 52-year-old patient of mine who I have repaired both shoulder rotator cuffs, the most recent one in the calendar year 2007.
2. While he was climbing a ladder recently in the immediate postop stage, he fell suffering the aforementioned heavily comminuted Frykman fracture.
3. This fracture had a fragment that extended in the distal radial ulnar joint, a die-punch fragment in the center of the radius.
4. The ulnar styloid and the radial styloid were off and there were severe dorsal comminutions.
5. He presented to my office the morning of April 3, 2007, having had a left reduction done elsewhere a day ago.
6. The reduction, although adequate, had allowed for the fragments to settle and I discussed with him the severity of the injury on a scale of 1-8, this was essentially an 8.
7. The best results have been either with external fixation or internal fixation, most recently volar plating of a locking variety has been popular, and I felt that this would be appropriate in his case.,Risks and benefits otherwise described were bleeding, infection, need to do operative revise or removal of hardware.
8. He is taking a job out of state in the next couple of months.
9. Hence I felt that even with close followup, this is a particularly difficult fracture as far as the morbidity of the injury proceeds.,OPERATIVE NOTE: , After adequate general endotracheal anesthesia was obtained, one gram of Ancef was given intravenously.
10. The left upper extremity was prepped and draped in supine position with the left hand in the arm table, magnification was used throughout.
11. The time out procedure was done to the satisfaction of all present that this was indeed the appropriate extremity on the appropriate patient.
12. A small C-arm was brought in to help guide the incision which was a volar curvilinear incision that included as part of this due to the fracture blisters eminent compartment syndrome and numbness in fingers.
13. A carpal tunnel release was done with the transverse carpal ligament being protected with a Freer elevator.
14. The usual amount of dissection of the pronator quadratus was necessary to view the distal radial fragment.
15. The pronator quadratus actually grasped several of the fragments itself which had to be dissected free from them, specifically the distal radial ulnar joint and die-punch fragment.
16. At this point, a locking Synthes distal radius plate from the modular handset was selected that had five articular screws as well as five locking shaft screws.
17. The ulnar styloid was not affixed in any portion of this repair.
18. The plate was viewed under the image intensification device, i.e., x-ray and the screws were placed in this order.
19. The most proximal shaft screw was placed to allow the remainder of the plate to form a buttress to then rearrange the fragments around the locking screws and a locking plate having been selected from the volar approach, a locking 12-mm screw through 16-mm screws were placed in the following order.
20. Most proximal on the radial shaft of the plate, then the radial styloid, i.e., the most distal and lateral screw, the next most proximal shaft screw followed by the distal radial ulnar joint screw.
21. Three screws were locking across the die-punch fragment.
22. The remaining two screws were placed into the radial shaft.
23. All of these were locking screws of 2 mm in diameter and as the construct was created, the relative motion of the intra-articular fragment in dorsal comminution all diminished greatly, although the exposure as well as the amount of reduction force used was substantial.
24. The tourniquet time was 1.5 hours.
25. At this point, the tourniquet was let down.
26. The entire construct was irrigated with copious amounts of bacitracin and normal saline.
27. Closure was affected with 0 Vicryl underneath the skin surface followed by 3-0 Prolene in interrupted sutures in the volar wound.

29. Screw lengths were changed out during the case as needed based on the x-ray findings.
30. The wound was injected with Marcaine, lidocaine, Depo-Medrol, and Kantrex.

Prior to each surgical stage, the surgical site was tested for anesthesia and reanesthetized as needed, after which it was prepped and draped in a sterile fashion.,The clinically-apparent tumor was carefully defined and debulked prior to the first stage, determining the extent of the surgical excision.
2. With each stage, a thin layer of tumor-laden tissue was excised with a narrow margin of normal appearing skin, using the Mohs fresh tissue technique.
3. A map was prepared to correspond to the area of skin from which it was excised.
4. The tissue was prepared for the cryostat and sectioned.
5. Each section was coded, cut and stained for microscopic examination.
6. The entire base and margins of the excised piece of tissue were examined by the surgeon.
7. Areas noted to be positive on the previous stage (if applicable) were removed with the Mohs technique and processed for analysis.,No tumor was identified after the final stage of microscopically controlled surgery.
8. The patient tolerated the procedure well without any complication.
9. After discussion with the patient regarding the various options, the best closure option for each defect was selected for optimal functional and cosmetic results.

=== #263 | McBride Bunionectomy & Wedge Osteotomy | Surgery ===
1. The patient was brought to the operating room and placed in a supine position.
2. The right foot was prepared and draped in usual sterile manner.
3. Anesthesia was achieved utilizing a 50:50 mixture of 2% lidocaine plain with 0.5 Marcaine plain infiltrated just proximal to the first metatarsocuneiform joint.
4. Hemostasis was achieved utilizing a pneumatic ankle Tourniquet placed above the right ankle and inflated to a pressure of 225 mmHg.
5. At this time, attention was directed to the dorsal aspect of the right first metatarsophalangeal joint where dorsal linear incision approximately 3 cm in length was made.
6. The incision was deepened within the same plain taking care of the Bovie and retracted all superficial nerves and vessels as necessary.
7. The incision was then carried down to the underlying capsular structure once again taking care of the Bovie and retracted all superficial nerves and vessels as necessary.
8. The capsular incision following the same outline as the skin incision was made and carried down to the underlying bony structure.
9. The capsule was then freed from the underling bony structure utilizing sharp and blunt dissection.
10. Using a microsagittal saw, the medial and dorsal very prominent bony eminence were removed and the area was inspected for any remaining bony prominences following resection of bone and those noted were removed using a hand rasp.
11. At this time, attention was directed to the first inner space using sharp and blunt dissection.
12. Dissection was carried down to the underling level of the adductor hallucis tendon, which was isolated and freed from its phalangeal, sesamoidal, and metatarsal attachments.
13. The tendon was noted to lap the length and integrity for transfer and at this time was tenotomized taking out resection of approximately 0.5 cm to help prevent any re-fibrous attachment.
14. At this time, the lateral release was stressed and was found to be complete.
15. The extensor hallucis brevis tendon was then isolated using blunt dissection and was tenotomized as well taking out approximately 0.5-cm resection.
16. The entire area was copiously flushed 3 times using a sterile saline solution and was inspected for any bony prominences remaining and it was noted that the base of the proximal phalanx on the medial side due to the removal of the extensive buildup of the metatarsal head was going to be very prominent in nature and at this time was removed using a microsagittal saw.
17. The area was again copiously flushed and inspected for any abnormalities and/or prominences and none were noted.
18. At this time, attention was directed to the base of the first metatarsal where a second incision was made approximately 4 cm in length.
19. The incision was deepened within the same plain taking care of Bovie and retracted all superficial nerves and vessels as necessary.
20. The incision was then carried down to the level of the metatarsal and using sharp and blunt dissection periosteal capsule structures were freed from the base of the metatarsal and taking care to retract the long extensive tendon and any neurovascular structures to avoid any disruption.
21. At this time, there was a measurement made of 1 cm just distal to the metatarsocuneiform joint on the medial side and 2 cm distal to the metatarsocuneiform joint from the lateral aspect of the joint.
22. At this time, 0.5 cm was measured distal to that lateral measurement and using microsagittal saw, a wedge osteotomy was taken from the base with the apex of the osteotomy being medial, taking care to keep the medial cortex intact as a hinge.
23. The osteotomy site was feathered down until the osteotomy site could be closed with little tension on it and at this time using an OrthoPro screw 3.0 x 22 mm.
24. The screw was placed following proper technique.
25. The osteotomy site was found to be fixated with absolutely no movement and good stability upon manual testing.
26. A very tiny gap on the lateral aspect of the osteotomy site was found and this was filled in packing it with the cancellous bone that was left over from the wedge osteotomy.
27. The packing of the cancellous bone was held in place with bone wax.
28. The entire area was copiously flushed 3 times using a sterile saline solution and was inspected and tested again for any movement of the osteotomy site or any gapping and then removed.
29. At this time, a deep closure was achieved utilizing #2-0 Vicryl suture, subcuticular closure was achieved using #4-0 Vicryl suture, and skin repair was achieved at both surgical sites with #5-0 nylon suture in a running interlocking fashion.
30. The hallux was found to have excellent movement upon completion of the osteotomy and the second procedure of the McBride bunionectomy and the metatarsal was found to stay in excellent alignment with good stability at the proximal osteotomy site.
31. At this time, the surgical site was postoperatively injected with 0.5 Marcaine plain as well as dexamethasone 4 mg primarily.
32. The surgical sites were then dressed with sterile Xeroform, sterile 4x4s, cascading, and Kling with a final protective layer of fiberglass in a nonweightbearing cast fashion.

34. The patient tolerated the anesthesia and the procedure well and left the operating room in stable condition.,The patient has been given written and verbal postoperative instructions and has been instructed to call if she has any questions, problems, or concerns at any time with the numbers provided.

18. This allowed us to actually seat a 20 cm plate contoured to the lumbar lordosis onto the pedicle screws all the way from S1 up to the T11 level.
19. Once we placed the plate onto the screws and locked them in position, we then packed the remaining BMP sponge and morselized autograft bone through the plate around the incomplete fracture healing at the L1 level and then dorsolaterally at L4-L5 and L5-S1 and L3-L4, again the goal being to create a dorsal fusion and enhance the interbody fusion as well.
20. The wound was then irrigated copiously with bacitracin solution and then we closed in layers using #1 Vicryl in muscle and fascia, 3-0 in subcutaneous tissue and approximated staples in the skin.
21. Prior to closing the skin, we confirmed correct sponge and needle count.
22. We placed a drain in the extrafascial space and then confirmed that there were no other foreign bodies.
23. The Cell Saver blood was recycled and she was given two units of packed red blood cells as well.
24. I was present for and performed the entire procedure myself or supervised.

=== #483 | Broviac Catheter Placement | Surgery ===
1. The patient came to the operating room and had an uneventful induction of general anesthesia.
2. We conducted a surgical time-out to reiterate all of the patient's important identifying information and to confirm that we were here to place the Broviac catheter.
3. Preparation and draping of her skin was performed with chlorhexidine based prep solution and then an infraclavicular approach to left subclavian vein was performed.
4. A flexible guidewire was inserted into the central location and then a 4-French Broviac catheter was tunneled through the subcutaneous tissues and exiting on the right anterolateral chest wall well below and lateral to the breast and pectoralis major margins.
5. The catheter was brought to the subclavian insertion site and trimmed so that the tip would lie at the junction of the superior vena cava and right atrium based on fluoroscopic guidelines.
6. The peel-away sheath was passed over the guidewire and then the 4-French catheter was deployed through the peel-away sheath.
7. There was easy blood return and fluoroscopic imaging showed initially the catheter had transited across the mediastinum up the opposite subclavian vein, then it was withdrawn and easily replaced in the superior vena cava.
8. The catheter insertion site was closed with one buried 5-0 Monocryl stitch and the same 5-0 Monocryl was used to tether the catheter at the exit site until fibrous ingrowth of the attached cuff has occurred.
9. Heparinized saline solution was used to flush the line.
10. A sterile occlusive dressing was applied, and the line was prepared for immediate use.
11. The patient was transported to the recovery room in good condition.
12. There were no intraoperative complications, and her blood loss was between 5 and 10 mL during the line placement portion of the procedure.

=== #619 | Radiofrequency Thermocoagulation - 3 | Pain Management ===
1. After proper consent was obtained, the patient was taken to the fluoroscopy suite and placed on a fluoroscopy table in a prone position with a chest roll in place.
2. The neck was placed in a flexed position.
3. The patient was monitored with blood pressure cuff, EKG, and pulse oximetry and given oxygen via nasal cannula.
4. The patient was lightly sedated.
5. The skin was prepped and draped in a sterile classical fashion.,Under fluoroscopy control, the waists of the articular pillars were identified and marked.
6. Local anesthesia infiltrated subcutaneously and deep extending down toward these previously marked points.
7. Once the anesthesia was established, an insulated 10-cm, 22-gauge needle with a 5-mm non-insulated stimulating tip was placed in contact with the waists of the articular pillars at the affected levels that were previously mentioned.
8. This was done under direct fluoroscopic control utilizing a gun barrel technique with PA views initially for orientation and then a lateral view to determine the depth of the needle.
9. For C3 to C6 medial branch RFTC's, the needles are placed along the ventral aspect of a line that connects the greatest antero-posterior diameter of the articular pillar but remains dorsal to the foramen as seen on lateral imaging.
10. For a C7 medial branch RFTC, the needle tip is positioned more superiorly such that it overlies the superior articular process.
11. For a C8 medial branch RFTC, the needle is placed at the junction of the superior articulating facet and the base of the transverse process of T1.,Sensory stimulation was carried out at 50 Hz from 0 to 2.0 volts.
12. Stimulation was stopped once the maximum voltage was delivered or the patient either described a buzzing sensation indicating that it was a nonpainful nerve, or it caused replication of their concordant pain.
13. The stimulation was then changed to 2 Hz for motor stimulation and advanced up to 2.0 volts or until motor stimulation was found at that level.
14. If motor stimulation occurred, the needle was repositioned to abolish it but still cause concordant pain, or the RFTC was aborted at this level.,If the sensory stimulation caused concordant pain without motor stimulation, the area was then anesthetized with 1 cc of Marcaine 0.5% with 5 mg of methyl prednisolone acetate.
15. Once the anesthesia was established, a radiofrequency lesioning was then done at 65 degrees for 60 seconds.
16. The same procedure was carried out at all the affected levels.
17. The patient tolerated the procedure well without any difficulties or complications.
